findings.where: Nav bar logo (top left) and the hero drawing, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The client's mark is changed. In the nav, both the arches and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark are white, not the logo's grey #404040 and blue #0070C0. In the hero, the mark's band-over-three-arches shape is drawn again in white, with an amber hatch laid into one arch. Mark has not supplied or approved a reversed (white) version.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo the brief says stays as it is and is never redrawn (client value 7, brand sheet §4). The house rule is never to recolour a logo: a white version is made only once the client says yes. Until then this is a clash for the founder to rule on.

findings.where: Hero: the amber-hatched third arch, and the amber 'WRITE TO MARK' button below it; the palette tile's Sodium Amber, 'daylight in the drawing, and the one action'
findings.fault: The colour kept for the one action also colours a decoration. The amber bay is the brightest spot on the first screen, so the eye goes there before it reaches the button. The hatched bay also looks highlighted or selected, as if it could be clicked.
findings.who_objects: The bank official scanning for what to do next. Two amber shapes compete for the job of the action, and the drawing wins on size and position. The house reserves the primary action's colour for the action.

findings.where: Nav bar title block: the 'DRAWING MMM-GA-001' and 'SCALE NTS' cells beside PROFILE / ARTICLES / BLOG / CONTACT; on phone they take the top row beside the logo
findings.fault: Two cells with no action are boxed exactly like the four nav links, in the same row and the same colour, so they look like menu items. On phone they take the first row, and the real links drop to a second row.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor who clicks 'MMM-GA-001' and gets nothing. On phone they also scan past a drawing number before reaching the menu. Parts that look the same should do the same thing.

findings.where: Hero name block: the circled 'A' and the line 'LONGITUDINAL SECTION A–A • SCALE NTS' under 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR'; also 'NTS' and 'EQ' on the drawing. On phone the line wraps with the bullet left at the end of a line
findings.fault: The line where a visitor looks for who Mark is, and what and where he advises, is half drawing-sheet jargon that is never explained. The circled 'A' reads as an avatar initial or a step marker, not a section mark.
findings.who_objects: The bank official, a lawyer or finance person rather than an engineer. 'Longitudinal section A–A, not to scale' tells them nothing and takes the place of facts that would help them decide (his practice areas, regions, the PPP law work). Task text should explain its technical terms.

findings.where: Whole identity: the engineering drawing sheet, Highway Gothic–derived type, drawing number and title block
findings.fault: The look says civil-engineering or design consultancy. Only the second paragraph says he is a lawyer who advises on PPP law. The sheet's voice is also a firm's and impersonal (a drawing register number, a title block), not one person speaking.
findings.who_objects: The official looking for an independent legal advisor on a PPP law, who could take this for an engineering firm at a glance. Also Mark, whose brief puts the individual ahead of a firm's voice (client value 1, brand sheet §5).

findings.where: First screen and the whole tile, desktop and phone
findings.fault: Mark is never seen: there is no photograph and no frame for one, not even a labelled placeholder. Nothing in the look shows where his face would sit.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who wants to know a real, named person does the work before writing to him (first-visit trust item 1). Also Mark's brief: 'the man himself… is seen and heard' (client value 3), which every tile must answer.

findings.where: Hero 'WRITE TO MARK' button (mailto) and the nav's 'CONTACT'
findings.fault: The only way to make contact is a mailto button. The email address never appears as readable text, and CONTACT goes nowhere yet.
findings.who_objects: An official on a locked-down bank laptop with no default mail program, or one who wants to copy the address into Outlook. A click that does nothing is the moment they give up. The house's contact rule asks for the full address as its own link text.

findings.where: Article specimen ('The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'), and every text block below the hero
findings.fault: The full blueprint grid of minor and major lines runs under the reading text. In a long article, lines cross every row of the text.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles, the site's Read mode, going through a 1,500-word piece on PPP law. The grid adds texture that tires the eye in exactly the mode where the ground should be quiet.

findings.where: Hero drawing: the thin S-curve rising off the right end of the ground line, and the amber hatch in the third arch
findings.fault: The curve at the right is not labelled and joins nothing, so it reads as a stray line. The hatch fills only part of the arch opening and leaves an empty sliver under the crown, so it looks misdrawn rather than meant.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who works on infrastructure and reads drawings for a living. In a look whose principle words are 'cut · measured · exact', loose linework undercuts the precision it claims.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the 'REPLAY THE CUT' button
findings.fault: The button is styled as underlined text, the look the page uses for links (as in the 'Streamlining the PPP Process' link). So a button and a link share one treatment.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined phrase to take them somewhere, not to replay something in place. Underlines are kept for links.

findings.fault: The 'EARTH HATCH' label and its hatched box sit hard against the panel's left edge with no padding. The poche box runs to the right edge, and an empty strip with no dimension line hangs below. The panel looks broken, unlike the same panel at desktop.
findings.who_objects: Mark or Angélique judging the tile on a phone. The texture is supposed to show precision, and here it looks unfinished.

findings.where: The whole sheet: a double outer frame, an inner frame, a rule under every eyebrow, a boxed texture panel, a boxed motion panel and a boxed PDF row
findings.fault: Boxes sit inside boxes inside a double border. Groups that space alone already separates also get lines, so the page reads as heavy with rules.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who found MacGeorge's site 'much too busy' and asked for nothing busy (client value 4). Every added frame takes away from the calm the drawing sets up.
